title: At the last month-end fix, currency hedges are resized by mandate and the size of the resizing is a public number: the month's equity return signs the euro's move through the 16:00 London benchmark

scout.mechanism: Cross-border equity investors hedge their currency exposure with short forwards sized to the portfolio's value, and the mandate says when to resize: at month end, at the benchmark. When US equities rise through a month, a euro-based holder of US equities has more dollar exposure than the hedge covers and must sell more dollars; the hedge ratio is a policy number in an investment management agreement, not a view. Unhedged investors rebalancing back to target country weights push the same way — outperformance means selling the winner and repatriating. Two different constraints, one sign. Crucially the resizing is executed AT the benchmark rather than around it: the whole point of a benchmark order is that the client's mark and the client's fill are the same number, so the flow is deliberately, contractually price-insensitive — the executor is instructed not to seek a better price. The size of the flow is not private either: it is a function of the month's equity return, which everyone can see, and of the stock of cross-border holdings, which changes slowly. So the claim is that the sign and rough size of a large, mandated, price-insensitive order arriving in a five-minute window on a known day are computable from a public number before the window opens. This is a mechanism and not a signal because the counterparty is forbidden by its own mandate from responding to price.
scout.why_unarbitraged: This is the weakest why_unarbitraged of the four proposals and it is written weak on purpose rather than dressed up. The flow is large enough that banks do trade it, publish month-end rebalancing estimates, and compete the front half of it away — so the honest claim is not that the effect is unknown but that a RESIDUAL survives, and there are structural reasons it must. (1) The forcer cannot stop. A fund that stops resizing its hedge at the benchmark is out of compliance with its own mandate; unlike an informed trader who can wait, it has to print. This is the cleanest possible instance of the brief's 'the forcer cannot stop'. (2) Benchmark execution is a service the client PAYS for — the executing bank's fee is for guaranteeing the fix price, so the bank's incentive is to internalise and hedge the flow, not to suppress the price footprint it creates. (3) The residual is small and lives in a five-minute window, so harvesting it requires taking directional risk into the most-scrutinised print of the month with a retail spread — a trade whose size is bounded far below the flow it is following. If this dies, it will die by being fully priced, and the falsifier is built to say so cleanly rather than to argue.
data_needed: data/bars/EURDUKA-1m.parquet — ON DISK: 5,881,397 minutes, 2010-06-01 to 2026-05-31, giving about 190 month-ends and two disjoint eight-year windows, which is the split every record in this loop uses.

NOT ON DISK, and trivially free: monthly total returns for the S&P 500 and the EURO STOXX 50 over 2010-2026 (Stooq serves plain CSV with no key; any equivalent pinned source is fine). The conditioning variable must be computable from information public BEFORE the window opens — month-to-date return through the previous close — and the registration must say so explicitly, because using the full-month return including the last day's close would be a look-ahead.

A London clock, with DST handled. The window is 15:45-16:15 London bracketing the 15:57-16:03 WM benchmark fixing window. The DST machinery already exists and is proven: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-venue-residual.md produced 'an alignment proof that is reusable (52 weeks, 0 disagreements, both feeds shifting on exactly the two NY DST weeks)'.

Vantage EURUSD costs from config/default.toml: spread 0.00014, i.e. 1.4 pips. That is the number that closed 2026-09-14-fx-local-hours, where the gate needed -0.7 pips of spread, so it must be charged in full here and the registration must state in advance what effect size would clear it.

NOT NEEDED for the first pass: cross-border holdings stocks (TIC, IMF CPIS). Scaling the signal by holdings would sharpen the size estimate; the first pass should use the sign and magnitude of the relative equity return alone, because a second data source is a second place to introduce a look-ahead.
scout.falsifier_sketch: Declare before the run: the conditioning variable is the month-to-date total return of the S&P 500 minus that of the EURO STOXX 50, measured through the CLOSE PRIOR to the last business day; the statistic is the ordinary-least-squares SLOPE of the 15:45-16:15 London EURUSD return on that variable across the ~190 month-ends of 2010-2026; the declared direction is a POSITIVE slope (US outperformance precedes euro strength through the fix) and no mirror is available. It dies if the slope is <= 0, if it fails the 95th percentile of a null that permutes the equity return across month-ends (which preserves the unconditional month-end drift and tests only the conditioning), or if the slope is positive and significant but implies less than 1.4 pips of move at the median absolute equity return — in which case the mechanism exists and is not a trade, and the record should say exactly that, as 2026-09-13-close-reopen-drift did. Three pre-declared placebos, each fatal on its own. (1) Day placebo: the same regression on the PENULTIMATE business day of each month must not produce the same slope; if it does, the day is not the variable and this is a monthly momentum effect. (2) Window placebo: the same regression on 13:45-14:15 London, a window inside European hours but containing no benchmark, must not produce it; this placebo is mandatory rather than optional because docs/decisions/2026-09-14-fx-local-hours.md established a real unconditional euro drift through European hours, and the fix window sits inside it — the closed effect is the most likely confound and it must be shown to be an intercept, not the slope. (3) Sign placebo: run the identical machinery on a month-to-date return of GOLD instead of equities; a slope there of comparable size means the conditioning variable is 'risk appetite' and the hedging story is decoration. Print the null's centre and a day-block interval beside every percentile; declare the draws (100,000) and state the minimum detectable slope before opening the window, because 190 observations is the sample size at which this loop has repeatedly failed to resolve an effect, and saying so in advance is the difference between 'no' and 'underpowered'.
scout.closest_known: docs/decisions/2026-09-14-fx-local-hours.md and its successor 2026-09-14-fx-local-hours-sign.md — the euro's European-hours drift, which passed every in-sample test at the 96th-100th percentile on 2,087 holds, needed -0.7 pips of spread to clear the gate, and then read 67th on direction on the unread window. That is the closest relative, it shares the instrument AND overlaps the clock window, and the distinction has to be stated plainly rather than assumed: that claim is an unconditional daily hold whose only variable is the hour, and its failure mode was that the hour stopped working in 2025. This claim holds the same instrument for thirty minutes on twelve days a year, and its variable is not the hour at all — the hour is held constant and the test is entirely in the SLOPE on an external public number. The overlap is real enough that placebo (2) above exists solely to prove the closed effect is not supplying the result. Second closest: docs/decisions/2026-09-13-london-fix.md, the other benchmark-window record in this repository — gold, the LBMA auction, unconditional, closed at the 74th-84th percentile. Same observation applies and is the reason both records are useful here: a benchmark window with two-sided flow does not drift, which is what that record found, and finding the day on which the flow is mandated one-sided is the only way such a window could carry anything.
